characterizations.result_summary: FTIR spectra of dried polyAMPS, polyAAM, and poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels were obtained, and the polyAMPS homopolymer structure was found to be independent of initiation mode.

evidence.source_sentence: FTIR spectra<sup>14</sup> <sup>–17</sup> of dried gels in the form of KBr discs containing 1%–2% polymer were obtained using a Bio-Rad model FTS-60 spectrometer.

Figure 10 FTIR spectra of (1-a) polyAMPS synthesized using free-radical initiation; (1-b) polyAMPS gel synthesized by gamma irradiation (8.5 kGy); (2) polyAAM synthesized by gamma irradiation (8.1 kGy); (3) and (4) poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gel synthesized by gamma irradiation at 2.3 and 50.8 kGy, respectively. Spectra have been offset for clarity.

The IR spectra of the dried poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels were very similar to those of the AAM–AMPS copolymers prepared by free-radical-initiated polymerization<sup>9,31</sup> and by initiation with a high-frequency discharge.<sup>12</sup> The FTIR spectrum of the gamma-initiated polyAMPS gel is shown in Figure 10, together with the spectra of free-radical-initiated polyAMPS, gammainitiated polyAAM gel, and poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels at low- and high-radiation doses. Comparison of the spectrum of polyAMPS in this work with reported spectra<sup>26,32–34</sup> of polyAMPS synthesized using various types of chain initiation indicates that the homopolymer structure is independent of the mode of initiation.

characterizations.result_summary: No reflections observed in XRD patterns of dried poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels, indicating no crystalline domains, consistent with random copolymerization and crosslinking.

evidence.source_sentence: Wide-angle X-ray diffraction patterns of dried poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels formed at doses of 9.0 and 50.8 kGy showed no reflections, implying absence of crystalline domains, which is consistent with random copolymerization and crosslinking.

characterizations.result_summary: Dried poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels exhibited homogeneous surface morphology across 2.2–50.8 kGy doses

evidence.source_sentence: A Philips XL30 scanning electron microscope was used to investigate the surface morphology of the dried gels.

SEM micrographs of the surfaces of dried poly(AAM– co–AMPS) gels with doses in the range of 2.2–50.8 kGy showed a homogeneous surface morphology at all doses, which can be attributed to the low concentration of the comonomers in the pregel solution and to short-range X-shaped crosslinks with zero-bridge chain length.

characterizations.result_summary: Two different water structures exist within poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels: bound (hydration, destructured) water and free (bulk, structured) water.

evidence.source_sentence: A previous study<sup>26</sup> using Raman spectroscopy and DSC showed two different water structures existing within poly(AAM–co–AMPS) gels made by free-radical-initiated polymerization: bound (hydration, destructured) water and free (bulk, structured) water.
